guide.summary: Authorization code OAuth lets the app call the GitLab API on behalf of the connected person, after the app is registered. The least-privilege documented grant that covers reading project issues is read_api, which gives read access to the API but not writes.

findings.title: Authorization code flow gives API access on behalf of the connected person
findings.detail: The OAuth access token lets the app make API requests on behalf of the user. Authorization code (with or without PKCE) is documented for server-side and client apps.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts connect through OAuth.

findings.title: read_api scope for read-only API access
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. Project issue listing is an API endpoint, so this grant supports reading issue titles. The token shows only what the connected person can already access.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with no create, update or delete calls.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.

steps.title: Register the GitLab OAuth application
steps.detail: Developer registers an OAuth application at the GitLab user settings Applications page with a Redirect URI and the read_api scope, then copies the Application ID and Client Secret. Use a user-owned application for individual customer accounts.
steps.doneWhen: The application shows an Application ID and a Client Secret, and the Redirect URI and read_api scope are saved.

evidence.quote: Enter a Name and Redirect URI .
Select Save application . GitLab provides:

fields: Redirect URI: your app callback URL (HTTPS in production)
Scope: read_api (no write scope)
Application ID and Client Secret are provided by GitLab after saving

steps.title: Send the connected person to GitLab consent and check the callback
steps.detail: Redirect the connected person to the authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state and scope=read_api. The person approves access and GitLab redirects back with code and state. Verify state matches the value you generated.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code and the same state value that was sent; the person sees the approval screen for read_api.

evidence.quote: Request authorization code. To do that, you should redirect the user to the

https://gitlab.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=APP_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE&scope=REQUESTED_SCOPES&root_namespace_id=ROOT_NAMESPACE_ID This page asks the user to approve the request from the app to access
The redirect includes the authorization code , for example:

fields: APP_ID: Application ID from the registered app
REDIRECT_URI: must match the registered Redirect URI exactly
STATE: random value generated by your app (CSRF protection)
The approval step is performed in a browser by the connected person

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the returned code to the token endpoint with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri and code. Response contains access_token, refresh_token and expires_in. This is an unexecuted authorization step; run it only after consent.
steps.doneWhen: The response includes access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

steps.title: Read the first page of project issue titles
steps.detail: Call the project issues endpoint with the access token and per_page=100 to list issue titles for a project the person can access. Use a documented project ID the developer provides. Read-only; no create, update or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a JSON array and each element has a title string; the Link header shows whether a next page exists. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: List all project issues
per_page Number of items to list per page (default: 20 , max: 100 ).
Pagination Link header Link headers are returned with each

fields: PROJECT_ID: a project the connected person can access, provided by the developer
ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the exchange step
per_page=100 is the documented maximum
Use --include so the Link header is visible for pagination

steps.title: Read the next page of project issue titles
steps.detail: Request the next page using the rel="next" URL from the Link header of the previous response, resolved against the same HTTPS instance host. Repeat until the Link header has no rel="next" entry or x-next-page is empty; that is the documented end of listing. Repeat the next-page request with the rel="next" URL from the latest response until the documented end condition is reached: no rel="next" Link header, or x-next-page empty.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is read until the response has no rel="next" Link (or x-next-page is empty), and total titles collected are reported. No rel="next" Link header remains and all pages are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
